patterns.note: Canonical runboard renderer and lifecycle mutation flow; render_runboard owns the query, Markdown table, and derived-file write.
Existing bulk aggregation of latest execution records into visible stage directories, with state-specific age sources.
Existing human-readable elapsed-time formatter with future-time clamping.
Runner timestamp-test pattern using fixed timezone-aware datetimes, fake connections, and exact output assertions.
Operational-age test pattern covering exact stale boundaries, future values, and constant query count.

similar_features.name: Mission Control stage rail and elapsed ages
Gate latency and stale review cards

risks.risk: There is no single persisted stage-last-changed field: execution, approval, event, and run timestamps represent different mutations, while runs.updated_at also changes for non-stage metadata.
Visible stages do not map one-to-one to stage_executions: split UI/UX phases share a directory and human-mode coding creates no execution row.
The runboard renderer has no focused behavior test, despite being a shared human and agent orientation artifact.
The existing 24-hour stale rule covers pending Mission Control review cards only; the runboard has no general stalled-versus-slow classification.

conventions: workflow/RUNBOARD.md is a generated view; refresh it with python pipeline.py runboard and never hand-edit it.
Persist timestamps as timestamptz and test timestamp output with timezone-aware UTC datetimes.
Runner behavior tests use stdlib unittest and fake connections where live Postgres is unnecessary.
Operational list views use bulk queries and map rows in memory rather than issuing one query per run.
